function: Learns when to update the RIS tile exclusion (switching off shadowed tiles) in RIS-assisted indoor VLC; the tile choice itself is closed-form (p. 5-6).
system: Indoor VLC, 4 ceiling APs, 1-8 mobile users, 1,500 reflecting RIS tiles per wall (mirror or liquid-crystal), 5x5x3 m room, visible-light band (p. 1, 3).
method: Soft actor-critic (maximum-entropy DRL), fully connected actor and critic networks, reward shaping; reinforcement learning trained on one wall, only the actor deployed (p. 7-8).
data_channel: Self-generated Lambertian LoS channel gain (Eq. 1) over synthetic indoor mobility trajectories; 100 training and 100 validation trajectories per layout (p. 4, 8).
test_conditions: Trained on one wall of one layout; validated on other walls and layouts R1-R3, and on a four times larger room R4 without retraining (p. 6, 11).
baselines: Non-learned fixed-interval update timing from exhaustive search (p. 10-11); no earlier learned method compared, only the proposed agent at several network sizes (p. 9).
metrics: Channel-gain enhancement eta, eta per decision update, cumulative reward, reduction of RIS power consumption and control signaling (p. 10).
complexity: Actor cost O(2+5Nstate+Nstate^2), at least 4418 FLOPs, stated as 4418 trainable parameters; 53.55 us on an STM32F107 chip (p. 8, 9, 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "we calculate the channel gain for each time slot in each trajectory". The channel is the authors' own Lambertian VLC model (Eq. 1) on synthetic trajectories; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel data is used for training or testing.
q2_support: p. 6: "during training, the actor solely relies on data from a single wall, but during testing and validation, it is evaluated across different walls and layouts"; p. 11: "deploying an agent trained in R2 directly in a room four times larger, R4".
q3_support: p. 10: "We compare our approach with a fixed-timing method derived from an exhaustive search". This is a non-learned baseline only; no earlier learned method for the same function is compared (the network sizes of Figs. 4-5 are variants of the proposed agent).
q4_support: p. 9: "The computational complexity of the deployed execution network on hardware approximates O(4418), requiring a floating-point computational requirement of no less than 4418 FLOPs"; the same page gives 53.55 us on an STM32F107 chip.
q5_support: p. 8: "There are 100 UE mobility trajectories used for training in each layout". The data come from the authors' own mobility and channel generator; no code or data link or DOI is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Title on page 1 is 'Concept-Drift Aware RIS Tile Management in Dynamic VLC Networks' with DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3471745, so the PDF matches. Borderline inclusion: the DRL agent learns only the timing of the RIS exclusion update (kappa, p. 6), while the optimal tile selection is closed-form (Solution 1, p. 5). It is kept as learned RIS configuration control (area 3; the abstract says the RIS controller deactivates tiles from channel conditions) and not as above_phy, since the decision is driven by measured RIS channel gain drift; the reviewer may confirm. The RIS is a VLC reflector (mirror array or liquid crystal tile), not a phase-shift RIS. The mobility model was compared with Phyphox measurements (p. 4) and its parameters come from real-world measurements (p. 8), but the channel data used for training and testing are synthetic, so q1 stays 0. The paper gives 1.30 x 10^4 learnable parameters for 64 input neurons (p. 9) and 4418 trainable parameters for the deployed agent (p. 11); both are stated.
